sb_prompt: SEE HOW THE OTHER CALLER FEELS ABOUT THE PROPOSAL THAT ALL YOUNG AMERICANS SHOULD SPEND A YEAR OR TWO DOING SOME KIND OF PUBLIC SERVICE
turns: Yeah, I guess I'm pretty skeptical about the whole idea. I mean, I've sort of made up my mind a few years ago that it just doesn't quite work for most folks.
Yeah, I get that. I'm sort of on the fence too. It just feels like everyone else is doing it already, so why make it mandatory?
I mean, I never did it myself, and looking back, I don't think it would have changed much for me anyway, you know? Just feels like a waste of time honestly.

Yeah, exactly. Like, what happens if you're just stuck with it? Doesn't mean you're going to suddenly find your life's purpose or anything. Seems like just another thing to check off a list, honestly.

Yeah, that's exactly what I'm saying. I mean, you go out there, you're just doing whatever they tell you to do, no say in what you're actually doing. It's like... well, my job at the grocery store, I'm just managing people and stock, but at least there's a paycheck and it's real life. If you just spend a year doing community service, isn't that just another job without the benefits?
Yeah, that makes sense. Like, if it's just mandatory, it feels less like serving and more like just another job without the benefits.

And look, I know people like it, you know? I've got a college degree and I see all these kids coming out of it with certificates and saying it changed their lives. But honestly, when you think about it, isn't it just a way to keep young people off the streets or maybe even a cheap way to get them to work for free? I don't know, it just doesn't feel right to force it on them.

Yeah, that's what I'm worried about too, you know? It feels like the government just wants free labor, to be honest. Like, if you're rich, you can just take a gap year and travel, but if you're poor, you're forced to work for free for a year instead? It seems unfair to me.

Yeah, it just seems like we're just teaching them to be workers, not citizens. And honestly, where do we draw the line? What kind of work? Cleaning streets? Waiting tables? It feels like we're just creating a new class of indentured servants.

Yeah, that's the thing, isn't it? Like, if you're doing it because you *have* to, is it really service anymore? I drive that bus every day, and I see kids who just want to give up. I feel like we're missing the point if we just force it.
I mean, if they really want to change how people think, they should make it voluntary first. Like, you can't force passion, man. That's just how life is.
Yeah, but I guess if you're trying to build character, forcing it might actually do the opposite.

Yeah, that's the thing. If you make it mandatory, the only thing you're building is resentment. I mean, I've seen kids my age in the store who would kill to take a year off just to figure out who they are, not because the state told them to, but because they actually had the choice to make that choice for themselves. If you force it, they're just clocking in, not serving.
Yeah, exactly, if you're just ticking boxes nobody's actually gonna learn anything real.
